1.title: Ancient Rome, Part 1
1.subtitle: From a wolf to the Rubicon · 753–49 BC
1.yt_title: How a Village Became Rome: Wolves, Gold and Elephants (Ancient Rome, Part 1)
intro: Nearly three thousand years ago, a few huts stood on a hill above the river Tiber.
Within seven centuries, the people who lived there ruled the whole Mediterranean.
This is the story of how a village became Rome. Part one: from the she-wolf to the Rubicon.
outro: A village became a republic, and the republic became the master of the Mediterranean.
But one man had just crossed a small river with his army. In part two: Caesar, Augustus, and the empire at its height.

2.title: Ancient Rome, Part 2
2.subtitle: From Caesar to Trajan · 44 BC–AD 117
2.yt_title: From Caesar to Trajan: Rome at Its Height (Ancient Rome, Part 2)
intro: The Republic is dying. Julius Caesar has crossed the Rubicon and taken Rome.
In the next hundred and sixty years, Rome gets its first emperor, its greatest buildings, and its widest borders.
This is part two of the story of Rome: from the Ides of March to the largest empire Rome ever ruled.
outro: From a murder in the Senate to an empire that stretched from Britain to Mesopotamia.
In part three: walls, crises, a new capital, and the long end of Rome.

3.title: Ancient Rome, Part 3
3.subtitle: From Hadrian to 1453
3.yt_title: How Rome Really Ended (Ancient Rome, Part 3)
intro: At its height, the Roman Empire stopped growing and started building walls.
Then came civil wars, a new capital on the Bosphorus, and the fall of the West.
This is part three of the story of Rome, and how it really ended, more than a thousand years later.
outro: From a hill above the Tiber to the walls of Constantinople: more than two thousand years of Rome.
Which empire should we sketch next? Tell us in the comments.
